The Community Development Block Grant program gives heavy emphasis to the improvement of park and community center facilities in the city. Major improvements are planned for Backesto Park (Northside CNRA), Woodrow Wilson Park (Gardner CNRA), the George Mayne School park (Alviso CNRA), Meadowfair Park (Evergreen), plus construction of or addition to the Mayfair Community Center (Mayfair CNRA), Northside Community Center (Northside CNRA) John XXIII Senior Center (Campus CNRA), Alum Rock Senior Citizens Center, and the Alma Neighborhood Center (Alma CNRA). In addition the C.D.B.G. program will help fund the Nihonmachi Community Services Program and expand the curb ramp construction program for greater mobility for the physically handicapped. All of these projects will have a major positive impact on the provision of park and social services to the community.
K. CULTURAL RESOURCES
The implementation of the C.D.B.G. program can have a positive impact on the identification and preservation of San Jose's cultural and historic past. Through the general up-grading of older neighborhoods and more specifically the rehabilitation of older homes, the earlier architectural character of San Jose will be enhanced. If in conjunction with the survey of historic districts, certain portions of target neighborhoods can be so certified, an added benefit to both historic preservation and neighborhood revitalization can be achieved. The tax incentives for rehabilitation in an historic district, plus the funding available through the C.D.B.G. program can have a very positive environmental impact. Prior to any demolition, subject buildings should receive individual assessment by the San Jose Historic Landmarks Commission to identify any unique historical, cultural or archaeological characteristics.
Of special importance is the C.D.B.G. program of Historical Preservation Loans, which will be available in the Alum Rock and Central Planning Areas. Under this program a maximum loan of $15,000 at a 7% interest rate would be available for residential structures designated as historically significant by city ordinance or state action. This program will be available in the 5th and 6th year only of the C.D.B.G. effort.
Three constructions are planned during the Community Development Block Grant program; the Alma Community Center and the expansion of the Carnegie Library in Olinder and the Alum Rock Senior Center. Additionally considerable trenching will occur during the laying of sewer lines in both Alviso and Gardner. The opportunity for discovering both prehistorical and historical resources exists in each situation. The Gardner, Olinder, and part of the Mayfair, Northside, and Alviso neighborhoods are archaeologically sensitive, as identified on the San Jose Planning Department's archaeological resource maps.
